# Review checklist (one essay)

Ordinary-English checklist for a person reviewing a draft against the **module brief** for **one essay id**. Use this before Word confirm or when giving feedback. It does not add doors, call a model, or send Slack.

Synthetic patterns in `docs/samples-study.md` inform briefs and rubrics only. **Do not** ask the writer to copy or match a sample draft or submitted answer.

For editing habits when the brief does not name a module writing guide, use `docs/academic-writing-helpers.md` (router for shared stages — referencing stays Harvard Referencing). Essay shape is `docs/essay-writing-helpers.md`. Report shape is `docs/report-writing-helpers.md`.

## On-brief structure and genre

- [ ] The question or task in the brief is answered directly.
- [ ] **Genre** matches the brief: **essay** (argument-led) vs **report** (headed sections, skim-friendly). See which helper to open in `docs/academic-writing-helpers.md`, then `docs/essay-writing-helpers.md` or `docs/report-writing-helpers.md`.
- [ ] Section order and headings follow the brief (report section plan, essay introduction–body–conclusion, or hybrid named in the brief).
- [ ] Voice and person match the brief (e.g. third person unless the brief allows otherwise).

## Sources and argument

- [ ] Each major claim is tied to **gathered** evidence for this essay id — uploads, assignment, or a local subject note that was read — not decoration.
- [ ] For a specific point, you can name **which source** supports it and where it appears in the gathered text (invent-forbid: no invented author, quote, page, or DOI).
- [ ] Where the brief asks for **alternatives** (options, scenarios, comparisons), the draft addresses them rather than a single unstated choice.
- [ ] Clarify answers from full research are framing only; they are **not** cited as evidence (`docs/memo-how-it-works-note.md`).

## Word count

- [ ] Body word count sits in the **band** named in the brief for this module (and any `word_rules` on the pack).
- [ ] If the brief says whether in-text Harvard citations count toward the band, the count follows that rule.
- [ ] If count is outside the band, a person has acknowledged it on the pack before Word confirm — the door does not waive the band by itself (`docs/workflow.md`).

## Referencing (Harvard Referencing)

- [ ] In-text citations and the reference list follow **Harvard Referencing** (`docs/referencing-harvard.md`).
- [ ] Reference list entries use gathered fields or honest free look-up fills on the same gathered source; missing locators stay blank rather than guessed.
- [ ] Figure and table source lines use author–year from gathered text, not bare URLs.

## Noted versus open (slice 2)

- [ ] The pack `conclusion` is the person’s choice: **`noted`** or **`open`** (`docs/memo-how-it-works-note.md`).
- [ ] **Noted** is only fair when gathered excerpts support the ending; thin support should stay **open**, not be quietly closed.
- [ ] A confidence or “percent sure” line is not proof; opened pages must carry the claim.
- [ ] If validation refused **noted**, the reviewer does not pressure the writer to invent support — redraft or stay **open**.

## Presentation (Word, when used)

- [ ] Cover carries programme, module code, counted words, and noted/open — **no** student name and **no** student number (`docs/workflow.md`).
- [ ] Preview and `.docx` tell the same story (no second body in the preview).

## Out of this checklist

This sheet is one reader's check. It does not require regulator reports or professional standards before the essay can finish.
